Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.164 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation
amount with interest from the respondents.

Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 04.02.2025 at about 7.00 am, he was driving the car bearing Reg No.KA-06-AB-7654, near Muthhumariyamma Temple, wherein the driver of the two wheeler beg. Reg. No.KA-03-JA-9616, drove it with in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Car from its behind, when the petitioner inquired the same with the driver of the two wheeler he dashed against the Car driver and caused the accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he has bared medical expenses.
Petitioner stated that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the he was hale and healthy and he is aged about 26 years and she was working as a driver and thereby she was earning Rs.70,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that he sustained grievous injury in the motor vehicle road accident and the vehicle belongs to respondent No.2 who insured his vehicle with respondent No.1 and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.54/2025 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such both are liable to pay the compensation and she prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they have appeared through their counsel and filed vakalath and written statement.

Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of the policy to the vehicle belongs to respondent No.2 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.2 admit that he is owner of the two wheeler and contend that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.
4. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 produced marked 13 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 13 and he is fully cross examined.
Respondents have not chosen to lead their evidence and their evidence is taken as nil.

5. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire records.
6. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 04.02.2025 at about 7.00 am, he was driving the car bearing Reg No.KA-06-AB-7654, near Muthhumariyamma Temple, wherein the driver of the two wheeler beg. Reg. No.KA-03- JA-9616, drove it with in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Car from its behind, when the petitioner inquired the same with the driver of the two wheeler he dashed against Karthik G vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25090588/
2 the Car driver and caused the accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition.?

7. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1 & 3: In the Affirmative Issue no.2: In the Negative Issue No.4: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 8. Issue No.1 to 3:- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, spot mahazars, sketch,
IMV report, wound certificate, final report which are at Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that is one Syed Haris S/o Syed Ahmed was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Further more,
Ex.P5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate, Ex.P7 is the final report.
In the cross examination of PW-1, nothing is elicited to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained grievous injuries in a road accident due to the involvement of the offending vehicle.

The aforesaid undisputed documents establishes the fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road accident involving the usage of a motor vehicle which belongs to respondent No.2.
10.

Petitioner has filed petition U/s 164 of IMV Act., which is no fault liability and structurally framed scheme for the swift relief for the injured in an accident and petitioner need not to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, he has to prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle.
In the cross examination of PW-1, nothing is elicited to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained grievous injury in a road accident.
Petitioner has complied the ingredients of section 164 of IMV Act,
Accordingly as per Section 164 of IMV act, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.2,50,000/-.
11. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% P.a.

Liability :
The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.
Accordingly Respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner forthwith.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record.
I am answering Issue no.1 & 3 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the negative.
13. Issue No.4:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.164 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.2,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.a. from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal forthwith.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash sheristedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
